unit.why: An anecdote told by the Seer of Lublin: R. Shmelke asked him to tug his sleeve if his Talmud study ever broke his devekut, which he never needed to do, and once R. Shmelke caught himself first.
unit.boundary_note: Part of a run of source excerpts on constant devekut; the previous division ends a teaching, and the next begins an unrelated excerpt on the death of the Rema of Fano.

stories.start_quote: וגם סיפר שהל ובלינר זצוקל״ה בהיותו
stories.summary_en: R. Shmelke asked his disciple the Seer of Lublin to tug his sleeves if deep study ever broke his devekut; the Seer reports he never needed to, and once, as he was about to, R. Shmelke turned and said he had already reminded himself.

quotes: שאין הרהצה״ק רר״ש נפרד מדביקות ח״ו גם בעת לימודו
tags.why: The story is about R. Shmelke's unbroken cleaving to God.

quotes: שאין הרהצה״ק רר״ש נפרד מדביקות ח״ו גם בעת לימודו
tags.why: It depicts his inner state of devekut.
Deep study of halakhah and Tosafot is the setting.

quotes: ורצה לנענע בבתי ידיו כפקודת רבו
בהיותו לפני הרהצה״ק ר״ר שעמלקא זצל״ה
tags.why: The relationship and duty between master and disciple drive the story.

quotes: וסיפר הלובלינר זצל״ה שמעולם לא נצרך
tags.why: The tale is framed as the Seer of Lublin's own account.
The tale illustrates R. Shmelke's spiritual virtue of constant devekut.

quotes: ומתוך כך פנה אליו הרר״ש ואמר לו
tags.why: R. Shmelke seems to sense the disciple's unspoken intention.
The tale is embedded in a homiletic compilation of sources on devekut.

missing_concepts: a disciple charged as a spiritual reminder to his master
